Atlanta region Interstates and Expressways · NPMRDS (INRIX) probe speeds, Jan–Dec 2025 · 1,295 directional TMC segments · generated 2026-10-26

The whole analysed freeway network at a glance: each segment colored by its typical weekday 5–6 PM speed relative to free flow (median of the year's weekday speeds in that hour), with the region's top-20 freeway bottlenecks (Regional Congestion Report ranking) marked. Use the other tabs to change the hour, the measure or the direction, or to look inside a corridor.

Esri, HERE, Garmin, © OpenStreetMap contributors, and the GIS User Community — drag to pan, scroll or use +/− to zoom. Click a segment for its details.

Top-20 freeway bottlenecks (regional report ranking)

The freeway bottlenecks ranked in the Regional Congestion Report (AADT-weighted severity index), at their peak segment. Click a row to see that freeway's time–space diagram.

Speeds are compared with each segment's own free-flow speed and grouped into fixed classes — the same breaks every run and every year, so maps and charts can be compared over time. The 70% break is the analysis's congestion threshold. The chart shows how many directional freeway miles fall in each class in each hour of a typical day. Click a bar to open that hour on the Time of Day map.

Typical conditions hour by hour. Drag the slider, use the presets, or press Play to watch congestion form and clear across the day. Weekdays and weekends are summarised separately (median speed in each hour), so holidays and unusual days don't dilute the peak.

Esri, HERE, Garmin, © OpenStreetMap contributors, and the GIS User Community — drag to pan, scroll or use +/− to zoom. Click a segment for its details.

Top-20 freeway bottleneck

How much delay, not just how slow. Color shows the average day's estimated vehicle-hours of delay per mile in the selected hour (directional NPMRDS AADT × hourly distribution × excess travel time); line width shows directional traffic volume. A busy road with a moderate speed drop can carry more delay than a quiet road with a severe one.

Sections with the largest difference between directions

A time–space diagram shows where and when congestion forms along one section: distance along the road runs left to right in the direction of travel, hour of day runs top to bottom. A recurring bottleneck is a dark patch that starts at a fixed point and grows to the left (upstream) as the queue builds; where it ends is when the queue clears. Hover a cell for its cross street and hour.

How to read this view. Every freeway is drawn as a wall standing on the map. Height = how much delay: vehicle-hours lost per mile in the selected hour on a typical day (more traffic and slower speeds both make a wall taller). Color = how slow traffic is compared with free-flow speed, using the same colors as the other tabs. Tall dark-red walls are where the most people are stuck in the slowest traffic. Press Play to watch walls rise into the evening peak and fall overnight. Drag to rotate · right-drag or Ctrl-drag to pan · scroll to zoom · hover a wall for details · click it to open Segment Detail.
The 3D view loads when this tab is opened.

Tallest walls this hour

Compare hours and roads directly. One player drives all three views: the road race shows which sections carry the most delay in each hour (one fixed scale for every hour, so bar lengths compare across the day); the heatmap shows every hour of the worst sections at once; the small maps show the whole network once per hour, side by side. Click any small map or heatmap column to jump to that hour.

Road race — most delay in this hour

Each bar is one section and direction. Delay per mile (default) ranks how intense the delay is, the same basis as the corridor rank, so long and short sections compare fairly; Total delay ranks how much delay a section carries in all, which favours long sections. Length = the chosen measure in this hour on a typical day, color = typical speed vs free flow. Click a bar for its time–space diagram.

The network hour by hour

Atlanta Regional Commission · CBI freeway analysis. Speeds: NPMRDS from INRIX, all 2025 days, typical condition = median of each hour's daily average speed (weekdays and weekends separately). Free-flow speed per TMC = INRIX reference speed, as in the corridor bottleneck analysis. Volumes: NPMRDS 2025 AADT split by direction. Annual delay = excess travel time x hourly volume over every day of the year (cbi_freeway_speed_conditions.py).
